matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compare the left‑hand side with the right‑hand side to find the difference.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before trying any stick moves, compute the numeric values to know how much the equation is off.
matchstick.example: In V = XVII - X, 5 vs 7 gives a discrepancy of -2.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all possible Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each character in the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, consider every numeral that can change by one stick.
matchstick.example: I can become II by adding a vertical; V can become X by adding a diagonal.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure the character you took it from remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and the character you added it to also becomes a valid one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X leaves V, which is still a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick can be moved from a V to make an X (value +5) or removed from an X to make a V (value −5); the rest of the symbol stays valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is a multiple of 5 and a V or X is present.
matchstick.example: Changing V to X adds 5 to the value.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical from II yields I (value −1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust a value by exactly one.
matchstick.example: Turning I into II adds 1 to the numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign, and adding a vertical to a minus creates a plus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy can be fixed by changing subtraction to addition or vice‑versa.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal, and vice‑versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, check that the orientation matches the target character.
matchstick.example: A diagonal cannot be placed to form an I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify that it now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning V into VI, recompute 6 = 16 - 10 to confirm correctness.

matchstick.title: Swap horizontal sticks between operators
matchstick.principle: A horizontal stick can be moved from one operator to another (e.g., from ‘=’ to ‘-’), turning the source operator into a minus and the destination into an equals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount and both ‘=’ and ‘-’ are present.
matchstick.example: Changing V = XVII - X to V - XVII = X by moving a bar.

matchstick.title: Move vertical stick from an I to create a new I adjacent to another numeral
matchstick.principle: A vertical stick from an I (or II) can be relocated to form a new I next to another numeral (e.g., after V to make VI, or after X to make XI), effectively shifting a value of 1 from one side of the equation to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±2 and an I is present that can be removed without breaking the remaining characters.
matchstick.example: In V = XVII - X, moving a vertical from the trailing I to the left V yields VI = XVI - X; moving it to the right X yields V = XVI - XI.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: Confusion between stick orientations; the model assumes any stick can be reoriented.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce the rule that sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal cannot become vertical.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the destination change and forgets to check that the source remains a valid numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always validate the source character after removal using the 'Validate source and destination characters' skill.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks operator transformations that involve vertical sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include operator change possibilities when enumerating single‑stick transformations.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the visual correction guarantees arithmetic correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move' skill before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming the equality sign cannot be altered
matchstick.why_it_happens: Misinterpretation that the '=' sign must stay unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that '=' can be transformed into '-' or vice‑versa by moving a horizontal stick, as covered by the swap‑horizontal‑sticks skill.
